newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crudes slump, diffs steady, Oman weakens.
newsitem.headline: Asian crudes slump, diffs steady, Oman weakens.

text.p: Outright values for Asian crudes tumbled lower on Monday in line with the crude futures sell off on Friday.
Spot market differentials were mostly steady, although traders said Oman may have slipped lower.
They said two majors traded a cargo at MPM -30 cents per barrel, down from the last deals heard at MPM -19 to MPM -23 cents.
However, brokers said the market was relatively quiet with most prompt trading already done and with players attending an oil conference in Kuala Lumpur.
The crude futures drop on Friday has steadied in late trading in Asia on Monday. SIMEX front-month Brent was last traded at $17.80, up 10 cents from London.
NYMEX front-month crude on ACCESS was last traded at $18.86, up seven cents from New York where prices had fallen 87 cents to $18.79.
Tapis swaps for July responded by dropping to $19.80/$19.95, down from $20.35/$20.45 on Friday.
July/August Tapis was flat and the third-quarter and fourth-quarter was traded at a 10-cent contango between two traders.
A Minas purchase by a Japanese refiner was clarified at a deep discount. A sale of 100,000 barrels was done at ICP -19 cents and a separate 150,000 barrels was sold at ICP -20 cents.
However, some traders assessed the market much higher, arguing the true value amid more limited supplies for June was flat to -10 cents.
